# onsemi’s Ferric deal separates closing cash from revenue-linked payments


By OpenTools Team


The planned acquisition targets package‑level voltage regulation for AI processors.


##


Closing and revenue milestones are separate gates


[onsemi’s November 2 agreement](https://www.onsemi.com/company/newsroom/news-and-insights/onsemi-to-acquire-ferric-establishing-leadership-in-power-delivery-for-next-generation-ai-processors) calls for $600 million in cash at closing and up to $175 million in additional cash if revenue milestones are met. Closing is expected by the end of 2026, subject to customary conditions.


The extra amount is a cap on contingent consideration, not guaranteed closing cash.


##


Power conversion at the processor


[The company describes integrated voltage regulation](https://www.onsemi.com/company/newsroom/news-and-insights/onsemi-to-acquire-ferric-establishing-leadership-in-power-delivery-for-next-generation-ai-processors) that places power conversion directly in the processor package or substrate. Ferric combines a power controller, transistors, inductors and capacitors in one compact package, onsemi says.


That is the architecture behind the AI‑processor power‑delivery strategy. onsemi plans to combine Ferric’s engineering with its own productization capabilities and scale.


ASUS motherboard voltage‑regulator area, November 2013; archive context, not Ferric or onsemi hardware or an AI benchmark.
